peon.title: Red-Green
peon.flow: A task moved to In Progress rolls to the Barracks; an orc takes it in its own worktree and works. Its finished patch rolls to the Orc Council, where a Diff Inspector and a Test Runner review it round by round until they agree; the verdict lands in the Loot Vault for you. When the Forge's tests go red, the failure rolls back to the Barracks and goes to the same orc. Meanwhile the Tally Crag sees the Forge pass its token cap and sounds the Horn.

timeline.what: Task Fields sends 'T2101 → In Progress'; a cart rolls to the Barracks, which turns BUSY (1 of 3 orcs).
The Tally Crag crosses its 150k-token cap; a cart rolls to the Horn.
The orc finishes; pool.done rolls to the Orc Council, which opens round 1 and agrees.
team.artifact_ready rolls to the Loot Vault: 1 to review.
The Barracks opens: the orc, the finished task and the foreman's reason for picking it.

patterns.name: Event-driven trigger
patterns.where: A status change on the board starts the work; nobody assigns it.

patterns.name: Orchestrator–workers
patterns.where: The Barracks' foreman hires or reuses an orc for each task and says why.

patterns.name: Prompt chaining
patterns.where: Task → code → review → verdict, each step's output is the next step's input.

patterns.name: Evaluator–optimizer
patterns.where: The Orc Council: reviewers object, the moderator revises, the next round reviews again.

patterns.name: Sticky assignment
patterns.where: Red tests from the Forge go back to the orc who wrote the code (forge.conflict → Barracks).

patterns.name: Human-in-the-loop gate
patterns.where: The verdict waits in the Loot Vault; Merge in the Forge is your key.

patterns.name: Bounded loop
patterns.where: The Council stops at 4 rounds or $2; the Barracks at $5; roads may not form a cycle.

patterns.name: Budget alarm
patterns.where: Tally Crag charts.threshold → the Horn.

knight.title: Night Watch
knight.flow: After a deploy the Watchtower reads the mail. A Totem sorts each message by rules, without a model: a Sentry alert goes to the Barracks, where an orc fixes the bug; the fix rolls to the Forge, which runs the tests and squash-merges it; the merge fires the Catapult at the deploy webhook. A refund request goes the cheap way: the Reply Mill fills a template and the draft waits in the Loot Vault. The Tally Crag watches the money and sounds the Horn past the cap.

timeline.what: A Sentry alert mail arrives; the Totem routes it to 'bug' and a cart rolls to the Barracks, which turns BUSY.
A refund request arrives; the Totem routes it to 'help'; the Reply Mill drafts an answer and the Loot Vault stores it.
Spend passes $3; a cart rolls from the Tally Crag to the Horn.
The orc reports 'fixed in fix/checkout'; the Forge tests and squash-merges fix/checkout into main.
forge.merged rolls to the Catapult, which fires (a dry run in the sandbox).
The Catapult opens: the POST to the deploy webhook with the merge in its body.

patterns.name: Event-driven trigger
patterns.where: Incoming mail, webhooks and a schedule start every run.

patterns.name: Routing
patterns.where: The Totem's rules send bugs and support mail down different roads, no model call.

patterns.name: Deterministic step instead of an LLM
patterns.where: The Reply Mill answers routine mail with a template: $0.

patterns.name: Orchestrator–workers
patterns.where: The Barracks takes the bug and hands it to an orc in its own worktree.

patterns.name: Prompt chaining
patterns.where: Alert → fix → tests → merge → release, each step feeding the next.

patterns.name: Quality gate
patterns.where: The Forge merges only when its test command passes.

patterns.name: Human-in-the-loop gate
patterns.where: Support replies wait in the Loot Vault; the Catapult can ask before each shot.

patterns.name: Budget alarm
patterns.where: Tally Crag spend cap → the Horn.

elf.title: Variants
elf.flow: A brief dropped into the Pit becomes work in the Barracks: orcs draw hero variants. A variant rolls to the Orc Council, where a Critic, an Accessibility orc and a Copy orc critique it until they agree; the agreed version opens in the Lake of Insight for you to look at. In the Loot Vault you reject a variant: it rolls back to the Barracks with the reason and goes to the orc who drew it. Accepted tokens go to the Token Mill, which turns them into CSS without a model.

timeline.what: The brief 'Hero section, 3 variants' drops into the Pit; a cart rolls to the Barracks, which turns BUSY.
The orc finishes hero-b; pool.done rolls to the Orc Council, which agrees in round 1.
team.artifact_ready rolls to the Lake of Insight: 'Hero B · Start free'.
hero-a is rejected in the Loot Vault; generator.rejected rolls back to the Barracks, BUSY again.
The Lake of Insight opens on the agreed Hero B.

patterns.name: Parallelization
patterns.where: The Barracks runs up to three orcs at once, one variant each.

patterns.name: Evaluator–optimizer
patterns.where: The Orc Council critiques by role and revises until all agree.

patterns.name: Human-in-the-loop gate
patterns.where: You accept or reject each file in the Loot Vault; nothing lands without it.

patterns.name: Feedback loop
patterns.where: A rejection rolls back to the Barracks with its reason (generator.rejected).

patterns.name: Sticky assignment
patterns.where: The send-back goes to the orc who drew the variant.

patterns.name: Deterministic step instead of an LLM
patterns.where: The Token Mill turns tokens JSON into CSS with templates.

patterns.name: Bounded loop
patterns.where: The Council stops at 3 rounds or $1; the Barracks at $3.

lich.title: Daily Status
lich.flow: Three sources feed one digest: the War Drum sends today's meetings, the Sprint Board sends task moves, the Watchtower sends its 09:00 tick. The Digest Catapult waits until all three have arrived, checks them and posts one digest to the team chat; a copy is kept in the Loot Vault. A review that has waited two days is caught by the Totem and goes to the Orc Council, which agrees on an unblock plan. When In Progress grows past its limit, the Tally Crag sounds the Horn.

timeline.what: The War Drum, the Sprint Board and the Watchtower each send a cart to the Digest Catapult.
All three are in: the Catapult fires the digest (a dry run in the sandbox); catapult.sent rolls to the Loot Vault.
'#41 review waiting 2 d' comes from GitHub; the Totem routes it to 'stuck' and the Orc Council starts.
In Progress reaches 7 of 6; a cart rolls from the Tally Crag to the Horn.
The Orc Council opens on the agreed unblock plan.

patterns.name: Scheduled trigger
patterns.where: The Watchtower's daily 09:00 tick and the War Drum's day schedule.

patterns.name: Fan-in (join / barrier)
patterns.where: The Catapult waits for all three sources (wait_for) before it fires.

patterns.name: Schema-checked output
patterns.where: The digest is checked against a JSON Schema before it is sent.

patterns.name: Routing
patterns.where: The Totem's rule picks out stuck reviews from the GitHub events.

patterns.name: Evaluator–optimizer
patterns.where: The Planner and the Critic agree on the unblock plan round by round.

patterns.name: Threshold alarm
patterns.where: Tally Crag tasks per column → the Horn.

patterns.name: Self-improvement, human-approved
patterns.where: Weekly, the stewards propose cheaper steps; nothing applies without your click (not in the clip).
